captions.detailed: A realistic bicycle crankset and pedal assembly featuring a dark grey bottom-bracket shell, a machined black spider and chainring, and two silver-grey crank arms pointing in opposite directions. Each crank arm is equipped with a rectangular black pedal body. The crank arms and chainring rotate continuously about the central axis of the bottom bracket, and both pedals are articulated to remain level during rotation.
captions.instruction: Generate a realistic bicycle crankset and pedal assembly. It must feature a dark grey bottom-bracket shell, a central rotating spindle, a machined black chainring with visible teeth, two silver-grey crank arms oriented 180 degrees apart, and two rectangular black pedals. Ensure the crank arms rotate continuously around the bottom-bracket axis, and the pedals maintain independent rotation on their spindle ends.
captions.factory: Define the bottom-bracket shell using a cylinder primitive. Construct the spindle and chainring (with teeth arrayed radially) as a single rotating assembly. Model the crank arms by extruding rounded rectangular profiles, placing them 180 degrees apart on opposite sides of the spindle. Create the rectangular pedals with small cylindrical axles, assembling them to the crank arm tips using revolute joints to allow independent leveling rotation.
